This is going to be short and sweet because I want it to be. I don't need a reason. I just tried my first jar of pickled tomatoes from August 20th.

Pickling spice: bad, make your own or don't use it, it's not good in most things you're going to use canned tomatoes for.

Sugar: a small amount doesn't seem to hurt it but I suspect you could do without this. The recipe I used called for 1:1:1 vinegar, sugar, water by volume, I went for maybe 33-50% less sugar. This is the sweetest I'd like it.

Vinegar/pressure canning: I would say there is a chance you may be better off doing pressure canning with less vinegar, vinegar didn't ruin the tomatoes by any means but you limit what you can use them for by making them so vinegar-y. This is something for me to try next year.

Salt: By all means go crazy with the salt if you like salty things. I would still recommend a large pinch to help preservation/flavor in general regardless

Overall the result was pleasing considering this was my first real round of canning ever. I'd rate the tomatoes 6/10 which doesn't sound amazing but it's perfectly acceptable, and I don't need to eat wetback greenhouse tomatoes all winter. Speaking of winter, it's been heading toward winter weather here with cool weather and lots of rain recently, my tomatoes may be done for extremely early this year. Thank fuck I canned and froze every single one that I could!
What I learned from canning my tomatoes
